newsitem.title: SOUTH KOREA: Seoul stocks end slightly higher, blue chips lead.
newsitem.headline: Seoul stocks end slightly higher, blue chips lead.

text.p: Seoul stocks closed slightly higher on Monday in light trading as core blue-chip counters led the market in the afternoon, brokers said.
They said the blue chip gain was seen as "technical" after losses last week.
The composite stock index closed up 3.76 points to 734.19 with just 25.8 million shares changing hands.

Despite the index rise, declining issues edged out advancers 375 to 365. Brokers said the market was generally viewed as fragile due to weak fundamentals such as lagging customer deposits and rising interest rates.
Among the blue chips, Samsung Electronics gained 500 won to 66,000 and SK Telecom was up 1,000 to 453,000.
Pohang Iron and Steel Co climbed 1,300 won to 58,100 on the news that its 1997 first half net profit had risen to 543.23 billion won against 385.83 billion a year ago, brokers said.
A company official attributed the surge in net profit to rising turnover and falling sales cost.
Brokers said uncertainty about the future of the struggling Kia Group would continue to be a big influence in the market.
Kia creditors were meeting on Monday to decide the group's future. Friday's meeting failed to reach an agreement.

"The outcome of the today's meeting will have a big impact on the market on Tuesday," said Baek Jung-hyun of Samsung Securities. "If the meeting is cancelled again, the market would fall back tomorrow."

Brokers said Kia Steel, an affiliate of the struggling Kia Group, closed at its limit up for the third trading day in a row following the news last week that Hyundai Motor Co and Daewoo Motor Co had agreed in principle to buy one-third stakes in Kia Steel.

Another Kia affiliate, Kisan, which added 410 won to its limit high of 5,610, and Asia Motors, up 20 won to 5,450, were the most traded stocks with 1.26 million Asia Motors shares and 896,360 Kisan shares changing hands.
Brokers said Kisan surged in anticipation of a third-party takeover.
Customer deposits, seen by brokers as a gauge of investor confidence in the stock market, were tallied at 3.01 trillion won as of August 1, down from 3.06 trillion on July 28.
"If the symbolic three trillion mark is broken, the sentiment would take another hit," said Lee Kye-joon of Daishin Securities.
Brokers said rising interest rates were another factor weakening investor confidence.
Yields on benchmark three-year corporate bonds closed Monday morning at 12.00 percent against 11.95 percent on Saturday.
